title: Sunny and the Dragonfly
description: Little Sonny the quokka watches a shimmering dragonfly dance above the creek. A shimmering, still bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny was sitting by the creek, watching the water, when something caught the light.

A dragonfly.

It hovered above the water, perfectly still in the air, its wings moving so fast they were almost invisible. Just a shimmer, a blur, a suggestion of wings. And the body — oh, the body. A long, bright needle of blue-green, gleaming like a jewel in the afternoon sun.

Sunny held his breath.

The dragonfly darted sideways. Stopped. Darted back. Hovered again.

It moved in a way that Sunny's eyes couldn't quite track. One instant it was here, the next it was there, as if the space between two places simply didn't exist for it.

He watched it patrol its little patch of the creek, back and forth, back and forth, lord of its own small world.

It landed briefly on a reed near Sunny's foot. So close he could see its enormous compound eyes — like two small faceted gems, seeing everything from every direction at once.

Then it was gone again, up and out over the water.

Sunny sat very still for a while after it had gone, the image of that blue-green shimmer still bright in his mind.

The creek ran on beside him. The afternoon light turned gold.

He felt, very quietly, like he had seen something important. Something that only happens when you are patient enough to sit and wait and look.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, shimmering dragonfly. Goodnight, patient and sparkling afternoon.
